betterquesting:10.desc:8: It's your first day. Better start punching trees and collecting resources.
I don't think the new neighbors like us very much. Better teach them a lesson.
Time to go mining and collect some metals and coal to move up the tech tree.
The Pulvus will allow you to double your ores, as well as grind down other items into their dusts, or cobble to gravel, and gravel to sand for example.

The Furnus is an upgraded furnace that can be further upgraded with modules that can increase the speed, fuel efficiency, and XP gain, as well as modules that allow you to reconfigure the input and output sides and process up to 3 items at once.

At this point, your chests are probably getting pretty crowded. Luckily, there is a solution - Iron Chests (and gold and diamond and more).

The Iron Chest is a double-chest size in a single block size. Further upgrades can add more storage, blast resistance, or the ability to see your items without opening the chest.

Cobblestone clogging up your chests? Storage Drawers are here to save the day.

Storage Drawers allow you to store large quantities of single items in one block space. They're available in single, double, and quad item varieties allowing you to store 32 stacks of 1 item, 16 stacks of 2 different items, or 8 stacks of 4 different items in a single block space.

They're also upgradeable for more (or less) stacks of storage, voiding excess, and more.

The Drawer Keys allow you to change functionality like locking them to their current item, showing the item, showing the quantity, etc.

This Backpack will allow you to store more on the go when you're out exploring or mining.

Place the Backpack on the ground and then sneak and break the Backpack to equip it. Set a hotkey in your controls to open it while equipped, or sneak+right-click the ground with an open hand to place the Backpack so you can open it.

The Workshop Table is an advanced crafting table that is very customizable.

The workshop allows you to install up to 4 crafting tables or furnaces, or any combination of the two. It also has an internal inventory to store crafting materials, and can be upgraded in many ways, such as speeding up or continuing to burn fuel to "charge" up for the next furnace operation.

Note: Crafting quest items in this table will not register for quest completion. Use a vanilla crafting table or the AE2 Crafting Terminal to craft quest items to ensure they are detected by the quest book.

Before we go much further, we're going to be needing some resources from the Nether.

Obviously, we'll need a portal to get there.
Mining is hungry work, so it's about time we start growing our own food supply.

Nobody wants to wait around for plants to grow, so a watering can will help us grow more food faster.

Growth Crystals don't hurt either.

At some point, you're probably going to collect enough cobblestone to last your lifetime, so this Portable Nullifier will auto-pickup up to a stack of the item you specify and then destroy any more that it picks up.

You can also make block forms of this to pipe items, fluids, and energy into if you have excess.

Gone out exploring and found something cool like a village or dungeon and forgot to mark it, or just don't want to make the trip?

Waystones are an easy way to get around the world. Whenever you find someplace you want to go again, just plop down a waystone, right-click it to activate it and give it a name, and then you can use your Warp Stone to go back there any time.

Of course, you'll want this Waystone to place at your base first or you'll have a long walk back.

Getting tired of going out mining or exploring and not being able to leave your machines to work for you while you do something else?

The Weirding Gadget is a chunkloader that will keep a 3x3 area of chunks around it loaded while you are away.

Note: If you are on a server, the Weirding Gadget will automatically shut off after 48 real hours. Just right-click it to start it again.
You probably have some stuff to cook by now, so let's get this one out of the way.

Storage Drawers are very useful, but you can make them even more useful with a few other blocks.

The Drawer Controller allows you to connect a wall of drawers together and access all the drawers from a single block.

The Compacting Drawer allows you to store items that can be crafted into a block and will allow you to access both the block and item at the same time (for instance - redstone and redstone block or iron ingot and block of iron).

It's about time to start thinking about expanding our resource processing to an industrial scale.

To get started, we'll need to build a Coke Oven to make coal coke and creosote oil.

The Coke Oven is a 3x3x3 multiblock structure that burns coal or coal blocks and turns them into coal coke or coke blocks with creosote oil as a byproduct. Smack it with your Engineer's Hammer to form the Coke Oven. Reference the Engineer's Manual for more information.

Note: This pack has Immersive Petroleum installed which adds Projectors for each of the multiblocks. The Projectors will project a ghost image of the multiblock into the world to aid in assembly if you don't want to keep referring back to the Engineer's Manual.
Now that we have some creosote oil, we can use it to make Treated Wood, which is needed to start making more advanced machines, as well as many other things.

The first step in making power is the Windmill, which will passively generate power using the wind.

You'll also need a Kinetic Dynamo to connect your Windmill so that the power can be extracted from the Windmill.

By making sails from hemp fibers, we can upgrade the Windmill to produce more power.

Just right-click the sails onto the center hub of your Windmill to install the sails.

Now that we have access to coal coke, we can start making steel, which is the next step to moving up in our technology level.

The Crude Blast Furnace is another 3x3x3 mutliblock that burns coal coke to turn iron into steel.

With the availability of steel, we can add to our power production with the Water Wheel.

The Water Wheel can be combined with up to 3 wheels to make power passively from flowing water over it. Like the Windmill, you'll need a Kinetic Dynamo to convert the water motion to power.

Now we're making power, but we need a way to move the power from our Windmill to the machines that need it.

Immersive Engineering adds 3 tiers of wires, connectors, and relays.

§1LV, or Low Voltage, wires can carry up to 2,048 RF/t, but connectors are limited to 256 RF/t in or out.
§2§5§3§6§7§8§9§d§2§a§5MV, or Medium Voltage, wires can carry up to 8,192 RF/t, but connectors are limited to 1,024 RF/t in or out.
§4HV, or High Voltage, wires can carry up to 32,768 RF/t, but connectors are limited to 4.096 RF/t in or out.

§0Where power enters and exits a network of wires, you'll need a connector. Since the wires have a distance limit, you'll also need relays to extend that range as well as at any point you want to connect multiple connectors to a single point since connectors can only have one wire connection.

To make everything look nice, there are posts and wallmounts you can craft to attach connectors, like real power lines.

You're not likely going to need all the power you're producing all the time, so why not be able to store some of it for later?

Like the wires, there are 3 tiers of Capacitor.

§1The LV Capacitor can store 100,000 RF.
§5The MV Capacitor can store 1,000,000 RF.
§4The HV Capacitor can store 4,000,000 RF.

§0Note: The input and output rates of the capacitors are limited the same as the connectors.

One of the first things we can use our new alloys for is the Thermoelectric Generator.

The Thermoelectric Generator creates power based on the heat differential between 2 blocks placed on opposite sides of the generator.

Try combinations of ice, snow, and water with things like lava.

Now that we're moving on to bigger and better machines, we're going to need ways to move items around.

The Conveyors will transport items and can extract and insert from adjacent inventories.

There are even conveyors with trapdoors to drop items in the world, vertical conveyors to move items straight upward, splitting conveyors to alternate the path, and covered conveyors.
The Assembler is a multiblock that can store items for and automatically craft up to 3 stored recipes, including recipes that use liquids.

Some of the more advanced machines will be needing more advanced parts - like gears, plates, and rods.

And while we can craft these by hand, the Metal Press can do it more efficiently and automatically.

You may even want several Metal Presses fitted with different molds so you don't have to swap molds around.

Note: You can use your Engineer's Hammer to rotate Pistons.

The Crusher is the first major piece of equipment on the road to industrial resource processing.

This large multiblock accepts ores and other blocks dropped into the top of it and crushes them down quickly into their dusts and automatically outputs to an inventory on the front (or a conveyor, hint hint).

The Improved Blast Furnace offers several improvements over the Crude Blast Furnace.

By reinforcing the blast bricks, we can make steel faster. Additionally, the Improved Blast Furnace will automatically export its slag and steel to adjacent inventories, and can be automatically inserted into from the top.
By attaching Preheaters to the Improved Blast Furnace and powering them, we can increase the heat and produce steel even faster.
The MV Capacitor can store 1,000,000 RF and as might be implied by its name, can also input and output more power than the LV Capacitor.
The HV Capacitor can store 4,000,000 RF and can input and output even more RF/t.

Another thing we're going to need for our more advanced machines are alloys. Alloys are combinations of 2 different metals that form a new metal.

Some examples are Electrum, which is a combination of Silver and Gold, and Constantan, which is a combination of Copper and Nickel.

The Alloy Kiln is a 2x2x2 multiblock that combines 2 metals into an alloy and is powered by coal.

The Garden Cloche is a self-contained farm. Simply provide it water, a seed and some dirt, and optional fertilizer and it will automatically grow and harvest crops.

Note: the Garden Cloche can also grow other crops that don't grow on dirt - some experimentation might prove beneficial.
The Fluid Pump can be powered to move fluids faster through connected pipes or to pump fluids from the world (like water and lava).
By swapping in different blueprints, the Engineer's Workbench allows you to create all manner of tools and items, including the Arc Furnace Electrodes and different projectiles for the revolver.

Now that we're building larger machines, they're going to need larger amounts of power. We should probably think about building a better generator.

That generator is the Diesel Generator, which can generate up to 4,096 RF/t. It burns biodiesel to generate power.

To make biodiesel, we'll need to refine plant oil and ethanol.

Plant Oil is made by squeezing seeds in the Industrial Squeezer.

As we upgrade our resource processing, we're going to need to look at gathering more resources more quickly for all that processing speed.

Although we don't have access to a full quarry, we can start off with the Excavator, which will dig up ores in the current chunk.

However, it doesn't dig up just any ore. In Immersive Engineering, each chunk is randomly generated with certain types of ores that can be excavated independent of the actual ores in the ground. To find out what will be excavated, place a Core Sample Drill in the chunk, power it, and wait a short time for it to drill a sample. The sample will tell you what the Excavator will dig up.

Tip: The Core Samples can be placed on the ground to remind you of what is in the chunk.

The Excavator is another massive multiblock that will dig up ores in the current chunk.

The Excavator consumes 4,096 RF/t, so you'll want to make sure you're producing enough power before hooking this beast up.

The other ingredient for biodiesel is Ethanol.

Ethanol is made in the Fermenter from crops like sugar canes, apples, potatoes, melons, etc.
The final step in making Biodiesel is refining the plant oil and ethanol in the Refinery.

Now we burn the biodiesel in the Diesel Generator.

The Diesel Generator produces 4,096 RF/t.

The Arc Furnace is a massive multiblock furnace that can smelt and double ores directly, make steel and other alloys, and do it all 12 at a time and much faster than almost any other furnace.

But it needs Graphite Electrodes in order to operate. To make the electrodes, you'll need to grind some coal coke down into dust and then squeeze the dust into HOP Graphite Dust and finally smelt the graphite dust into HOP Graphite Ingots that can be formed into the electrodes.


Each electrode requires 4 HOP Graphite Ingots to make and the Arc Furnace needs 3 electrodes to function.
Time to seriously upgrade your resource processing. The Arc Furnace smelts up to 12 items at once and can make steel and other alloys faster than any other machine so far.

By now, you've probably got overflowing chests and walls of drawers. Wouldn't it be nice to be able to store all your stuff in an easily accessible system?

Enter the ME System from Applied Energistics 2. AE2 allows the creation of a computer system that can store all your items on disks, as well as facilitate auto-crafting, interface with machines and inventories, and more.

To start with, you'll need a supply of Certus Quartz, the basic crafting material of AE2. Certus Quartz is found as ore underground.

Many of the components and items you'll need to craft for your ME system will need Charged Certus Quartz Crystals, which are used to make Fluix Crystals.

Rarely, you'll run across Charged Certus Quartz ore underground, which will give you Charged Certus Quartz.

The more advanced machines and items will need Fluix Crystals, which are made by tossing a Charged Certus Quartz, a piece of Nether Quartz, and a piece of Redstone into a puddle of water and waiting a moment for them to combine.

Additionally, to make life easier in the future, AE2 has a Charger that can be used to charge normal Certus Quartz.

In order to build your ME system, you're going to need to be able to make processors. And in order to make processors, you'll need the appropriate presses in order to form the 3 different chips and the printed silicon needed to make them.

Presses can be found in chests in the center of meteors that have fallen to the ground.

Onward and explore for meteors!

Hint: if you need a pointer in the right direction, there is a meteorite compass that can be crafted and will point you toward the nearest meteor (which may not always be on the surface).

While Certus Quartz isn't particularly rare, you are going to need a lot of it as you build out your ME system. Grinding up your certus quartz crystals and combining the dust with sand will give you 2 seeds, which when thrown in water, will grow into Pure Certus Quartz crystals, doubling the amount of certus quartz you have.

You can also do the same with your Fluix Crystals.

However, this process takes a long time, unless you have power. Surrounding your puddle of water with these Growth Accelerators will significantly speed up the growth of your certus and fluix seeds.

The Inscriber uses the Presses you found earlier to make the printed chips and silicon needed to make processors. They're also used to combine the printed chips and silicon with redstone to make your processors.

The Inscriber is somewhat limited in that it can only accept one item per slot at a time, and only from specific sides depending on which slot it is intended to be inserted.

While the standard puddle of water surrounded by Growth Accelerators works, it's a bit of a challenge to automate and can't be sped up any further.

The Crystal Growth Chamber fixes those problems. Insert your seeds and they'll grow in the safety of the enclosed chamber, which can be further sped up with acceleration cards.

The Advanced Inscriber solves the problems of the standard Inscriber by allowing you to insert stacks of items at a time for processing, as well as inserting and extracting from any side you want.

You can also lock the top and bottom slots if you want to set up dedicated Advanced Inscribers for specific processors.

The ME Controller is the brains of your system.

Each side of the controller can support 32 channels. Each device you connect on a cable will consume one channel. Standard cables can carry 8 channels, while dense cables can carry the full 32 channels, but most devices won't connect directly to dense cables.

These ME Controllers can also be combined in a freeform multiblock to give more channels and more points of connection for your cables.

Note: There can be only one ME Controller or ME Controller multiblock per ME system. If you want to add more controllers, you must add them onto the existing controller or controller multiblock.

You'll need a lot of these processors for your cells, controllers, interfaces, and more.

Logic Processors are made from Gold, Calculation Processors from Pure Certus Quartz, Engineering Processors from Diamonds, and the Printed Silicon is made from silicon which is smelted certus quartz dust.

Combine a printed circuit with a printed silicon and redstone in the Inscriber to make your processor.

Next up, you'll need a place to keep the storage cells that your items will be stored on.

The ME Drive can accept up to 10 storage cells of any size and will indicate the cells' fullness via LEDs on the front.

This is your basic storage cell (or disk) for your ME system.

ME Systems store items in a unique way:

A storage cell can store up to 63 unique types of items (like Iron Sword or Gold Ore).

The 1k Storage Cell can store up to 65 stacks worth of those 63 items, or it can store up to 127 stacks of a single item.
The 4k Storage Cell can store up to 260 stacks of 63 unique items or 508 stacks of a single item.
The 16k Storage Cell can store up to 1,040 stacks of 63 unique items or 2,032 stacks of a single item.
The 64k Storage Cell can store up to 4,160 stacks of 63 unique items or 8,128 stacks of a single item.

Now that you have some patterns, you need some place to put them.

The ME Interface is the answer. 

The Interface can be placed next to a machine and patterns placed inside it so the ME System can access the connected machine for processing. This can be used for things like pulverizing ores and smelting items, as well as much more.

You can also have the Interface keep items in stock and available to be extracted. This is useful for keeping an attached furnace full of fuel for example.

The block form of the interface can also be used to insert the results of crafting back into the system, or as an import into the system from other operations that aren't connected directly to the interface.

The Interface can also be crafted by itself in a crafting grid to turn it into a part form to be used where space is a concern. Note however that you cannot connect item pipes or conduits to the part version.

The ME Interface Terminal will allow you to see the patterns in all of your connected interfaces from one location.

Besides connecting Interfaces to machines for processing, you can also connect them to Molecular Assemblers.

Molecular Assemblers are auto-crafters for standard crafting table recipes.

You can also upgrade the assemblers with acceleration cards to craft items even faster.

Note that you can connect multiple Interfaces to a single Molecular Assembler for more pattern storage, or multiple Molecular Assemblers to a single Interface for faster and parallel crafting.

You can also use the assemblers as single pattern crafters by setting the pattern in the assembler and then pumping items in.

In order to access your system, you'll need various types of terminals.

The basic ME Terminal will allow you to insert and extract items.

The ME Crafting Terminal allows insertion and extraction, as well as providing a 3x3 crafting grid that can access the items in your system.

The first step on the journey to autocrafting is the ability to setup patterns so your ME system knows how to craft things.

The ME Pattern Terminal will allow you to create 2 types of patterns - standard 3x3 crafting table patterns and processing patterns so your system can use machines to process items.

You'll also need a bunch of Blank Patterns to write the recipes onto.

Of course, you're going to need some way to connect all your ME system components together, so there are many cables available for just that purpose.

The cables can be dyed different colors and will only connect to cables of the same color or to the fluix cables.

You can also add wool to make covered cables if you don't like the bare glass look. And then add redstone and glowstone to make smart cables that will display the channels in use on that cable run on the cable itself (more on that later).

Like the standard cables, these cables come in different colors and can be made smart as well.

The main difference is that dense cables can carry 4 times as many channels as the regular cables.

If you're tired of having to go back to your terminals to access your ME system, the Wireless Terminal will do what it says on the tin.

You'll need a Wireless Access Point to enable wireless on your ME System and a Security Terminal in order to link your Wireless Terminal to your ME System. The Wireless Booster cards are used in the Access Point to increase the range of your wireless signal, but they consume exponentially more power the more you add.

As a side note, you can use the Security Terminal and Biometric Cards to give or restrict access to other players if you're playing on a server.

The standard Wireless Terminal doesn't allow you to craft on the go, and is limited to the same dimension. The Wireless Crafting Terminal adds a crafting grid and can be used across dimensions with the Infinity Booster card.

It can also be upgraded with a Magnet Card that will auto-import items you pick up into the ME System based on its filter.

The ME System uses its own power (referred to as AE power). But, you can use other sources of power for your system by using the Energy Acceptor to input RF power.

Note: the Immersive Engineering cables/connectors will not input power into the acceptor directly. However, you can use an intermediate cable between them to input the power generated by IE, such as a Universal Cable from Mekanica.

If you like the look of the Immersive Engineering wires, then have I got good news for you!

You can also run cables for your ME system using ME wires that function similarly to the IE wires.

Note that these wires can't be dyed different colors.

To be able to autocraft, your ME system will need some extra memory in order to process the crafting request.

The Crafting CPU is a multiblock structure that is made up of at least 1 Crafting Storage, and can optionally contain multiple more Crafting Storage, Crafting Co-Processors, and a Crafting Monitor. It must be a cuboid shape.

The Crafting CPU will only consume one channel on your network, regardless of how large the Crafting CPU is.

The more complex the crafting operation is, or the more of it you request, the more Crafting Storage space you will need. When you request an autocraft in the system, the system will preview it and inform you if you have the required materials, but also the required Crafting Storage space and an available Crafting CPU.

Adding more Crafting Storage will increase the complexity and the total amount you can request at once.

Adding more Crafting Co-Processors will increase the number of parallel operations that can be performed.

Adding a Crafting Monitor will show the current item being crafted by the Crafting CPU.

Crafting Storage modules are available in the same sizes as your basic storage cells (up to 64k).

They can also be combined in any combination in your Crafting CPU, so you don't have to worry about useless 1k Crafting Storages laying about.

betterquesting:10.name:8: How Many Items Do You Need?
betterquesting:10.desc:8:
The Extra Cells mod adds storage cells all the way up to 16,384k.

How many items do you really need to store?
Extra Cells also adds the ability to store fluids in your ME System so you can access them directly, or use them for autocrafting.
Extra Cells also adds the ability to store gases in your ME system so you can access them directly, or use them for autocrafting.
To access your stored fluids, you'll need the fluid equivalents of the standard terminals and buses.
To access your stored gases, you'll need the gas equivalents of the standard terminals and buses.

In addition to the ME Interface, there are a few other parts that can be used to connect to other machines and inventories.

The ME Storage Bus can attach to a chest, drawer, drawer controller, etc. and effectively extends your ME system by adding that inventory as accessible to the system without importing those items into the system.

The ME Import Bus imports items from the connected inventory into the system. This is a very useful part when combined with, say, an Ender Chest and Ender Pouch.

The ME Export Bus exports items from the system into the connected inventory or machine.

Need more mob drops, but hate dealing with actual mobs? Woot has got you covered.

Woot is a mob farm that generates mob drops from thin air using lots and lots of power. It comes in several tiers that limit which mobs you can spawn, and can also be upgraded in a multitude of ways.

To get started, you'll need a Ya Hammer and a Stygian Iron Anvil.

The Tier I Woot farm can spawn common overworld enemies like creepers, skeletons, and zombies, but can also spawn passive mobs like cows and pigs.

Use the Factory Layout block to show a ghost of the blocks necessary to build the farm. Right-clicking on the guide will increase the tier displayed. Reference the Woot Guide book for a list of the blocks needed.

To form the farm, you'll also need a programmed Mob Controller using the Ender Shard.

The Tier I farm supports up to 2 Tier I upgrades.

The Tier II Woot farm will allow you to farm Nether mobs like Blazes, Ghasts, Zombie Pigmen, and overworld mobs like Witches.

The Tier II farm supports up to 4 Tier II upgrades.

The Tier III Woot farm will allow you to farm Endermen, Guardians, Villagers, and Wither Skeletons.

The Tier III farm supports up to 4 Tier III upgrades.

The Tier IV Woot farm will allow you to farm Wither bosses and Ender Dragons.

The Tier IV farm supports up to 4 Tier III upgrades.

Note that to spawn these mobs, you'll need to provide extra items to the farm for each cycle of the farm. For Wither bosses, you'll need 4 Soul Sand and 3 Wither Skeleton skulls per cycle, and for Ender Dragons, you'll need 4 End Crystals per cycle.
The Rate upgrades decrease the cycle time of the Woot farm. Each upgrade increases the power required.
The Looting upgrades increase the number of drops on each cycle of the Woot farm. Each upgrade increases the amount of power required.

The XP upgrades allow the Woot farm to generate experience in the form of XP Shards that can be consumed by right-clicking with them in hand, or sneak+right-clicking to consume the entire stack in hand. Each upgrade increases the power required.
The Mass upgrades increase the number of "mobs" generated on each cycle of the farm. Each upgrade increases the power required.
The Decapitate upgrades increase the chances of a mob head drop. Each upgrade increases the power required.
The Efficiency upgrades reduce the power required for each cycle of the farm.

Walking around is tiring and dangerous, and warping around is no good for exploring.

Airships are the explorer's preferred method of transport these days.

There are also other styles of Airships available - they all have the same starting stats and can be upgraded in the same ways.

Our basic Airship isn't so great, but luckily we can upgrade it.

We'll start with the Frame Upgrade. The frame upgrades allow further upgrades to our Airship.

Note: There are 5 tiers of each upgrade.

The Core upgrade increases the speed of the Airship.

The installed Frame upgrade must be the same tier or higher.

The Balloon upgrades increase the maximum altitude that the Airship can reach.

Once again, the installed Frame upgrade must be the same tier or higher.

The Engine upgrades increase the efficiency so you burn less fuel.

And again, the installed Frame upgrade must be the same tier or higher.
The Altitude modules further increase the maximum altitude of the Airship, but also increase the speed at which you climb.
The Speed modules increase both your forward speed as well as your turning speed.
The Efficiency modules increase the burn time of your fuel allowing greater range.

The Storage modules add onboard storage so your Airship can carry your luggage.

All that added weight will slow you down though.

Note: Although all the types of modules can be installed (storage, speed, altitude, etc.) only one can be active at a time.

These Wireless Connectors allow you to connect portions of your ME system wirelessly across larger distances instead of running cables.

Use the Wireless Setup Kit to connect the connectors at either end together.

Note that this uses a lot of power and the power requirements increase with distance. Also, this will NOT work across dimensions.

The End is home to many treasures, including the Elytra, but first you'll need to deal with the Ender Dragon.

Note: You can attach your Elytra to your chestplate in an Anvil. Just be sure your chestplate doesn't break, or you'll lose your Elytra.

Next up, Nether Stars.

You might also get some other fancy items.

Mekanica is an advanced tech mod that adds a lot of cool machines, generators, and tools that enable advanced resource processing and power generation.

With Mekanica you can produce up to 5 ingots per ore, produce millions of RF/t, and parallel process up to 7 items at once.

The first step is to get a Metallurgic Infuser, which allows you to infuse Iron and Osmium ingots with Redstone to produce Enriched Alloy and Basic Control Circuits respectively.

The Alloy can be further infused with Diamonds and Refined Obsidian to make more advanced alloys for more advanced machines and upgrading your circuits to more advanced versions.

The Enrichment Chamber functions as an ore doubler, producing 2 dusts per ore.

It can also be used to improve the efficiency of your Metallurgic Infuser. Placing redstone, diamonds, refined obsidian dust, or coal into the Enrichment Chamber will make a Compressed version of these items which will infuse 8 items each versus the 1 item for the un-enriched version.
The Energized Smelter is pretty self-explanatory - it's a powered furnace!

The Crusher is used to crush ingots and diamonds into dust, crush cobblestone into gravel, gravel into sand, and sand into silicon.

It's also used to crush organic materials into Bio Fuel, as well as being an integral part of the more advanced ore processing chain later on.

These Universal Cables can transfer large amounts of power. And they look neat too!

Note: You can also upgrade cables in place by right-clicking on a cable with the next tier of alloy. For example, Advanced Cables can be upgraded to Elite Cables by right-clicking on an Advanced Cable with a Reinforced Alloy. Also note that this will upgrade up to 8 cable segments at a time with one alloy. If you use an alloy on a shorter segment, it will still upgrade, but you will "waste" some material since the alloys can upgrade up to 8 cables each.

These Energy Cubes can store massive amounts of power - up to 51.2 million RF.

And that's not even the largest energy storage Mekanica offers...

But we have to start somewhere. This Basic Energy Cube will store up to 800,000 RF.
These Mechanical Pipes can transfer large amounts of fluids very quickly, and without the use of a pump.
These tanks can store up to 112 buckets of fluid and are portable - they'll keep their contents when broken.
Mekanica's advanced ore processing makes extensive use of various gasses. You'll need these Pressurized Tubes to move it around.
As you start making various gasses, it might be useful to store some for later, or have a buffer. These tanks can store up to 512 "buckets" of gas.
These Logistical Transporters can transport up to 2 stacks of items at a time nearly instantly.
These Bins can store up to 4,096 stacks of a single item.

Mekanica machines are upgradeable in many ways.

The most common upgrades are Speed and Energy upgrades. You can install up to 8 Speed and 8 Energy Upgrades in machines that accept them.

Each speed upgrade will increase the operating speed of the machine, but also increase the power required.

Each energy upgrade will decrease the amount of power required per operation.

The Muffling Upgrade will muffle the sounds produced by the machine while it is operating. You can install up to 4 of these in machines that accept them.

There are other upgrades available, and if you check the Upgrade screen in a machine, it will tell which upgrades it will accept.

The Basic Tier Installer will upgrade a machine in place to the Basic Factory version of the machine.

The Basic Factory version of a machine will be able to process 3 operations at the same time.

Note: you can also pick up your machines and craft the Basic Factory version using the machine as part of the recipe.

Upgrading your machines to factories will also increase their power requirements.

The Advanced Tier Installer will further upgrade your Basic Factory to an Advanced Factory that can process 5 operations at once.

Once again, this will increase the power required by the machine.

The Elite Tier Installer upgrades your Advanced Factories to Elite Factories that can process 7 operations at once.

And again, more power is required.
The Bio-Generator can burn Bio Fuel to make power. Bio Fuel is made by crushing organics in the Crusher.
This Solar Generator produces power from sunlight. Of course, that only works during the day.
The Advanced Solar Generator produces more power from sunlight, but still only works during the day.
This Wind Generator produces power from wind, and produces more power the higher it is.

The Gas-Burning generator can burn excess gas to produce power.

It can run on nearly any gas produced by Mekanica, including Hydrogen, Oxygen, and Ethylene.

Now that we have some basic Mekanica infrastructure, we can look at increasing the yield of our ore processing.

In order to get 3 ingots per ore, we need to add Oxygen into a Purification Chamber with our ore which will produce 3 ore clumps per ore. These clumps are then processed in a Crusher to produce 3 dirty dusts which are processed in an Enrichment Chamber to produce 3 dusts which can be smelted into ingots.

To get Oxygen for our Purification Chamber, we'll need an Electrolytic Separator which will take water and split it into Hydrogen and Oxygen.

In order to move up to 4 ingots per ore, we'll need to setup Brine production.

Brine is used in the production of Hydrogen Chloride which we need for quadruple ore processing.

Brine is made in the Thermal Evaporation Plant, a large multiblock structure (4x4x up to 18 high) that uses heat and water to create Brine.

The Thermal Evaporation Plant is affected by the biome it is located in for heat production and heat retention. Hint: Deserts are good.

To build your plant, start by building a 4x4x1 platform of Thermal Evaporation Blocks and then building up a hollow tower from there up to a max height of 18 blocks. Replace 2 of the blocks anywhere in the structure with Valves so you can input water and extract Brine. Place the Advanced Solar Generators at the corners of the top layer. Finally, replace any block, except corners, with the Thermal Evaporation Controller.

If everything is placed correctly, you should see red particles when it forms.

The Advanced Solar Generators on top will passively heat the plant, but you can increase the heat generation, as well as keep it hot at night, by pumping in heat from the Resistive Heater (which converts RF power to heat) or the Fuelwood Heater (which burns fuels to produce heat) through a Valve.

Now that we have Brine, we can start adding onto our triple ingot production to do quadruple ingot production.

First up, we'll need an Electrolytic Separator to process the Brine into Sodium and Chlorine. Then, we combine the Chlorine with Hydrogen in a Chemical Infuser to make Hydrogen Chloride.

The Hydrogen Chloride is pumped into a Chemical Injection Chamber with our ores to produce 4 ore shards per ore. These shards then go into our existing triple ore processing setup to be made into ingots.

Moving up from 4 ingots to 5 ingots per ore is a rather involved process that starts with the production of Sulfuric Acid.

We'll need a supply of Gunpowder for this process as Sulfur is extracted from Gunpowder. Gunpowder can be crafted by placing Gravel in a Purification Chamber with Oxygen to create Flint and then Crushing the Flint into Gunpowder.

Insert your Gunpowder with Hydrogen Chloride into a Chemical Injection Chamber to make Sulfur.

Process the Sulfur in a Chemical Oxidizer to make Sulfur Dioxide and combine that with Oxygen in a Chemical Infuser to make Sulfur Trioxide.

Create Water Vapor with a Rotary Condensentrator supplied with water and then combine the Sulfur Trioxide with the Water Vapor in a Chemical Infuser to produce Sulfuric Acid.

Now is the time to master the processing of ores. Adding our Sulfuric Acid to the processing chain will allow us to produce 5 ingots per ore.

To start, place your ores in a Chemical Dissolution Chamber with the Sulfuric Acid. This will produce an ore slurry.

The ore slurry is then combined with water in a Chemical Washer to produce a clean ore slurry.

The Chemical Crystallizer processes the clean ore slurry into ore crystals, which are then processed into the previous 4 ingot setup.

Congratulations, you are now making 5 ingots per ore!

The Precision Sawmill increases the yield from logs, giving you 6 planks instead of 4. It also produces sawdust as a byproduct which can be used to make paper or the Cardboard Box.

It can also be used to recycle some wooden items back into planks.

Some more advanced items can be created using Refined Obsidian Ingots or Glowstone Ingots.

To make these, you'll need to combine glowstone dust or refined obsidian dust with osmium in the Osmium Compressor.
Armor and Tools made from Refined Obsidian provides better protection and more durability than diamond.

The Digital Miner is a short range filterable quarry.

It can dig up anything within a 32 block radius and can also be set to fill in the holes of what it mines as long as you supply it with blocks. It can even silk touch blocks, although this increases the power required dramatically.

It has a powerful filter system than can filter on ore dictionary type, item/item stack type, materials, and by mod. When filtered, the miner will only dig up what is set in the filter, leaving the terrain intact.

Like all the other Mekanica machines, it can be upgraded as well.

Environmental Tech adds several different multiblock void miners and a solar array.

The Void Resource Miner produces blocks like stone, granite, andesite, etc., as well as the resources needed to upgrade the tiers of miners and solar.

The Void Ore Miner produces ores like iron, copper, osmium, coal, redstone, etc.

The Void Botanic Miner produces organic materials like wood, flowers, and crops.

Just place a chest next to or on top of the controller and provide power into the controller, and as long as the laser has a clear path to bedrock, the void miners will generate resources.

The Solar Arrays produce larger amounts of power the higher tier they are and when using upgraded photovoltaic cells.

This handy Assembler can be used to both assemble the multiblocks using the blocks in your inventory by holding right-click on the controller, as well as give you information about the current structure by left-clicking on the controller including telling you what blocks are needed to build the current tier and what blocks are needed for the next tier.
The Tier 2 Miner is a larger structure that can also accept modifiers.
Another larger structure that can accept more modifiers.
The next step up.
One more step up.
The biggest and baddest resource miner. Are you sure you need this much stuff?

The higher the tier, the more power the miner uses, but also the faster it operates.

Higher tiers can also make use of modifiers that can further speed up the miner or help the miner target specific resources in combination with different colored lasers.
The Tier 2 Miner is a larger structure that can also accept modifiers.
Another larger structure that can accept more modifiers.
The next step up.
Another step up.
The biggest and baddest ore miner. Good thing you can process these quickly.
Like the resource miner, higher tiers will use more power and operate faster, and can be upgraded with modifiers.
The Tier 2 Miner is a larger structure that can also accept modifiers.
Another larger structure that can also accept more modifiers.
The next step up.
Another step up.
The biggest and baddest botanic miner. Do you really need that many flowers?
As before, higher tier miners will operate faster and use more power, as well as being upgradeable with modifiers.
A larger solar panel that produces more power.
An even bigger solar panel that produces even more power.
Guess what? It's an even bigger solar panel!
You get a solar panel! And you get a solar panel!
The biggest and baddest solar array, as long as you have the best solar cells.

Each tier of Solar Array is larger and produces more power than the previous tier. But unlike the miners, each tier can be improved with better solar cells that produce more power without upgrading the tier.

The resources for upgrading the solar cells come from the Void Resource Miner.

The Configurator is the wrench of Mekanica.

It has many different modes, including wrench mode which can be used to instantly break machines and cables/pipes, rotate mode which can be used to rotate machines, and modes specific to resource types (such as item, fluid, gas, etc.) that allow you to set various sides of machines for those inputs and outputs or manipulate the cables and pipes directly to force input/output.

Check your keybinds and ensure you have a key set for the Mekanica Item Mode Switch in order to change the mode of the Configurator.

The Core Sample Drill can also tell you if an Oil Reservoir is present in a chunk. If there is one, the Pumpjack can be used to extract the oil.

You can also setup multiple Pumpjacks to extract the oil even faster.

The Distillation Tower is used to process Crude Oil into several different products.

Diesel can be used in a Diesel generator to produce power, as a replacement for Biodiesel.

Gasoline can be burned in the Portable Generator to produce power on a smaller scale.

Lubricant can be used with the Automatic Lubricator to speed up certain machines.

Bitumen can be used to make Asphalt Concrete, a dark decorative alternative to standard concrete.

The Portable Generator burns Gasoline to produce power at 256 RF/t. It has an internal buffer of 100,000 RF and will retain both its charge and its fuel when broken.

It also doesn't require a connector or relay; you can attach a wire directly to it.

The Lubricant produced from your Crude Oil can be used in an Automatic Lubricator to speed up certain machines by 25 percent.

This can be applied to the Crusher, Excavator, and Pumpjack.

Holding the Automatic Lubricator in your hand will show a ghost of the correct placement when looking at the relevant machines it can attach to.

Note: You can also use Plant Oil in place of Lubricant, but Plant Oil is less efficient. It takes 4 times as much Plant Oil to achieve the same result as Lubricant.

Ever wanted to swap a lot of blocks out at once? Well, with this handy Exchanger, you can swap up to 5x5 blocks out for blocks in your inventory.

To use, charge up the Exchanger, then sneak+right-click a block in the world to set the block to place, then look at the block you want to remove and you'll see an outline around the range of the Exchanger. Right-clicking again will Exchange the blocks provided you have enough in your inventory.

If exchanging 5x5 blocks at a time is too slow, this MV Exchanger might be able to help you out. It can do up to 11x11 blocks at a time.

Additionally, it will hold 5 times as much power, so you can exchange more blocks before needing a recharge.

If 11x11 is still too slow, this HV Exchanger can do up to 15x15 blocks at a time.

Additionally, it will hold 5 times as much power as the MV Exchanger, so you can exchange all day long without a recharge!

This Charging Station can be used to charge up any handheld items that require RF to run, such as the Exchangers.

Simply right-click the Charging Station with the item to charge in your hand and it will place the item in the Charging Station. While the item is charging, the tubes on the front will animate red. When they change to green, your item is charged and you can right-click the Charging Station with an empty hand to remove your charged item.

Cobblestone, Stone Bricks, and Sandstone are kinda limiting for aesthetics.

Luckily, you have many more options.

The Chisel mod allows you to chisel blocks into different textures, including stone, dirt, metals, redstone, and diamond blocks.

The Chisels and Bits mod allows you to break down and place pieces of blocks down to the pixel level. You can use it to combine the pieces of several different blocks to get the look you want. You can also use it for simple tasks like making covers for cables and pipes. You will also want at least one Chiseled Bit Bag to store all the pieces of the blocks you work on.

As you start building up your base, you may find these platforms useful. They can be used as scaffolding, catwalks, even rail beds! And you can make them out of most woods, stones, and metals.

To start, you'll need a Monkey Wrench and a PlatFormer.

The PlatFormer is the crafting table for platforms. Use the arrows next to the preview to scroll through the types of platforms, scaffolds, etc. to select the one you want to craft. Place the materials you want to use in the inventory at the bottom and then click one of them into the 2 slots to the left of the preview to set which material will be used. As long as you have available materials, you can pull out your platforms in the output slot.

The Monkey Wrench can be used to rotate placed platforms, as well as enable and disable handrails on walkways.

Note: to make metal platforms, use ingots, not blocks.

Similarly to the LV, MV, and HV Exchangers, these Exchangers will swap blocks with blocks in your inventory, but are made with Mekanica materials.

You can charge these the same way as your other Exchangers, or place them into the "plus" slot of an Energy Cube for much faster recharges.

The difference between these Exchangers and the IE-based Exchangers, is that the top 2 tiers of these Mekanica Exchangers can hold far more power, so you can exchange far more blocks before a recharge.

Looking for something even more renewable than Biodiesel?

Then the Steam Turbine is for you. The Steam Turbine uses the Steam produced from the Boiler or Solar Tower to produce energy.

This power generator starts off by using the Distiller to create Distilled Water.

Note: Although the Distiller is optional, it is more efficient.

In order to produce Steam, you can use either (or both) the Boiler or the Solar Tower.

The Solar Tower is used to create Steam from either water or distilled water. It requires at least one Solar Reflector to function.

Distilled Water is more efficient than regular water.

These Solar Reflectors are used to direct the energy of the sun into the Solar Tower in order to create Steam.

Although you only need 1 for the Tower to function, it can accept up to 4 at each cardinal direction up to 10 blocks from the Tower.

Note: This quest only requires the materials for one Reflector, so if you want all 4, be sure to create 4 times as much material.
Now that you have steam, you need a way to convert that steam to energy. The Steam Turbine is the first step - it takes the steam and uses it to rotate its large turbines.

Finally, build this Alternator next to your Steam Turbine in order to convert the rotational energy of the turbine into power.

Note: The Alternator connects to the protruding block of the Steam Turbine at the central steel block of the Alternator.

If you don't fancy using the power of the sun to generate your steam, this Boiler can do it for you.

Note: The Boiler requires fuel in the form of Biodiesel or Diesel.

It's probably better to keep your distance from the neighbors. After all, they can't hit you if they can't see you.

More cartridges can be made in the Engineer's Workbench.

You can also apply upgrades such as a larger magazine and a bayonet to your Revolver in the Engineer's Workbench.

Sneak+right-click to reload your Revolver and right-click to fire.

The Chemthrower can be used to spray liquids around the world.

It can be useful for building, but also for defense.

Like the Revolver, there are various upgrades you can apply to your Chemthrower in the Engineer's Workbench, like a larger tank, a better nozzle, and the ability to store multiple fluids.

The Gun Turret and Chemthrower Turret can be useful for providing automated defenses while you're busy building your factory.

Just be sure they don't run out of ammunition while you're not looking.
Thin the zombie horde.
Teach these block thieves a lesson.
Turn back the green invasion.

The Railgun is a long range weapon that fires Rods (like Iron and Steel Rods) as ammunition.

It also requires power to function and can be upgraded in the Engineer's Workbench.
The Advanced Energy Cube can store up to 3,200,000 RF.
The Elite Energy Cube can store up to 12,800,000 RF.
The Ultimate Energy Cube can store up to 51,200,000 RF.

The Induction Matrix is a multiblock structure made up of 4 components - Casings, Ports, Providers, and Cells.

The Induction Matrix can be up to 18x18x18 in size, and requires at least one provider and one cell. All edges of the structure must be casings, but the faces can be any combination of casings and ports.

Induction Ports are the blocks used for input and output from the Matrix. You'll probably want at least 2 of these - one for input and one for output.

Induction Cells are the blocks that actually store the energy. These are placed inside the structure and can be of any tier, even differing tiers. The capacities of all the cells are added together to determine the maximum capacity of the Matrix.

Induction Providers are blocks that determine how much energy can be output from the Matrix per tick. If multiple providers are present, their transfer rates are added together to create a total output rate for the Matrix - note that this is not per port, but for the whole Matrix. Similarly to cells, you can use differing tiers of providers. Also note that it is not required that the providers be placed next to the ports.

The interior of the Matrix does not need to be filled with cells and providers - as long as one of each is present, the Matrix multiblock will form and you should see red particles when that happens.

The blocks required for this quest will build the smallest possible Matrix with a single provider and cell and 2 ports.

It's time to amp up your power production with your very own Fusion Reactor.

To get started, we'll want to setup the production chain to produce the fuels needed to sustain the reaction.

First up - Deuterium, which is produced by running Heavy Water through an Electrolytic Separator. Heavy Water is obtained by running an Electric Pump over a water source with the Filter Upgrade installed.

The other fuel we need is Tritium.

This one is a little more involved to produce.

First, you'll want to build another Thermal Evaporation Plant, but instead of feeding it water, you'll want to feed it Brine. When Brine is processed in the Thermal Evaporation Plant, it produces Liquid Lithium.

Next, process the Liquid Lithium into Lithium gas in a Rotary Condensentrator.

Finally, process the Lithium gas in a Solar Neutron Activator to produce Tritium.

While D-T Fuel can be used directly in the reactor, it's far better to use Deuterium and Tritium separately in your reactor in order to sustain the reaction.

However, we'll still need a small amount of D-T Fuel loaded into a Hohlraum in order to kickstart the reaction.

The Chemical Infuser will combine Deuterium and Tritium into D-T Fuel. Placing an empty Hohlraum into the center slot of the Chemical Infuser will load the D-T Fuel into the Hohlraum.

Tip: Since we only need a small amount of D-T Fuel, it may be worthwhile investing in a Gauge Dropper. The Gauge Dropper can be used to pick and place up to 1000 mb of fluids/gases from one machine to another.

Besides the Hohlraum with D-T Fuel, the other thing we need to kickstart the reaction is a very large infusion of power very quickly.

The Laser Amplifier collects the power of up to 5 Lasers aimed at it and stores it. The Amplifier can be controlled with redstone, so it can be triggered when enough power has been stored.

For reference, the initial energy requirement is somewhere in the neighborhood of 600,000,000 to 800,000,000 RF.

Now, we build the Reactor itself. It might be worthwhile to reference the Mekanism Wiki for reference pictures on the build structure as it is a unique shape.

Note that the above is the bare minimum - you'll probably want at least one more port since we are using 2 fuels. Ports can be placed in Layers 2 and 4 in the center of each side, or any block except a corner in Layer 3.

Set up your Laser Amplifier so that it is pointing into the Laser Focus Matrix. Set up the Lasers pointing into the Laser Amplifier and supply them with power to begin building up your initial charge.

The Ports are used for both inserting fuel and extracting power, so connect up your sources of Deuterium and Tritium, as well as your power cables.

Insert the filled Hohlraum into the slot in the first tab of the Reactor GUI. Set the Injection Rate on the Fuel tab (start with the minimum of 2). Higher injection rates produce more power, but require more fuel.

When all is ready, fire your laser. Assuming you had enough power stored, the Reactor should fire up and start producing power. Once the reactor is running and stable, you can disconnect your lasers.

The Mining Drill is a fast mining tool that excavates a 2x2 area at once. It runs on Biodiesel.

The Iron Drill Head allows the drill to mine up to the Redstone level. The Drill Head does take damage over time and will need to be replaced eventually.

Install the Drill Head in the Engineer's Workbench, just like any other upgrade. To fuel up the drill, place the drill in the top right slot in the Refinery.

The Steel Drill Head increases the mining level of the drill to Obsidian and the mining area to 3x3.

The Additional Augers upgrades increase the mining speed of the drill and can stack up to 3.

These Hopper Pipes allow you to extend a hopper's output wherever you need it. When placed, there is an arrow on the pipe indicating the direction of travel.

The Filter Hopper allows you to set up to 5 items in the bottom row as whitelist items to filter through the hopper. Give it a redstone signal and the filter becomes a blacklist.

The Item Faucet is a sort of reverse hopper - it will take items from the connected inventory and dump them out into the world. Giving the faucet a redstone signal will stop the faucet. Depressing the handle on top will reverse this behavior (giving a redstone signal will start the faucet).

betterquesting:10.name:8: More Items Than You'll Ever Need
betterquesting:10.desc:8:
The Creative Vending Upgrade will give you unlimited item withdrawals when installed in a drawer.

Hint: You'll want an OSS (Object Submission Station) to submit the items. Place it and right-click to open the GUI, then select the quest and pipe in your items.

Additional Hint: You can set up multiple OSSs to submit multiple items simultaneously.

betterquesting:10.name:8: More Fluids Than You'll Ever Need
betterquesting:10.desc:8:
This creative fluid tank will allow infinite amounts to be withdrawn once given a bucket to set the fluid.

Hint: You'll want an OSS (Object Submission Station) in order to submit the fluids. Right-click the block, set the quest, and then pipe in the requirements.

Additional Hint: You can set up multiple OSSs for the same quest, all submitting different things simultaneously.

betterquesting:10.name:8: More Gases Than You'll Ever Need
betterquesting:10.desc:8:
This Creative Gas Tank will provide infinite amounts of whatever gas is set via pipes or dropper.

Hint: You'll want an OSS (Object Submission Station) in order to submit. Place the block and right-click to open its GUI. Select the quest and then pipe in the requirements.

Additional Hint: You can set up multiple OSSs to submit multiple requirements simultaneously.

Note: Gases are a bit of a unique beast, so this quest accepts the liquid forms of some later gases. The Rotary Condensentrator can be used to convert between liquid and gas forms.

The Paxel is a combination pickaxe, axe, and shovel, saving you valuable space on your hotbar.

Note: this quest requires the Mekanica Iron Paxel.

betterquesting:10.name:8: More Power Than You'll Ever Need
betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Need to take the awesome power of your reactor on the go? This Creative Energy Cube will provide an infinite amount of power.

Note: It can be crafted with itself to cycle between the Creative Energy Cube, Creative Capacitor, and Creative Energy Cell.

Hint: You'll want an OSS (Object Submission Station) in order to submit the items. Place it and right-click to open the GUI, then select the quest and pipe in the items.

Additional Hint: You can set up multiple OSSs to submit multiple items simultaneously.

This Mining Multitool will allow you to create a portal to a superflat, always day, peaceful mining world.

Just craft the tool with stone bricks to create the portal blocks, then build a portal the same shape as a standard Nether portal (minimum 10 portal blocks). Right-click the portal with the multitool to light it, then sneak inside the portal to go to the mining dimension.

This multblock tank can store up to 512 buckets of fluid.

It can insert or extract from the top or bottom, but requires a redstone signal to start the extraction and a Fluid Pump to extract.

The Silo can be used to store large amounts of a single item - up to 24 chests worth! That's 41,472 items!

Items are piped into the top and can be extracted from the bottom. Extraction requires a redstone signal to be applied to the silo.

If you're tired of constantly having to mine coal for your furnaces, the External Heater can be used to power a vanilla furnace instead of coal. As a side benefit, it will also slightly speed up the furnace operations.

Note: The External Heater does not work on the Furnus.

The Dynamic Tank is a multiblock fluid storage tank that can be from 3x3x3 up to 18x18x18 in size, and doesn't have to be a cube.

Each block of the tank, as well as each block of space inside provides 16 buckets worth of storage size. This means that the minimum tank size will hold 432 buckets of fluid and the maximum size is a whopping 93,312 buckets.

To build one, all the edges must be Dynamic Tank blocks, but the faces can be any combination of Dynamic Valve, Dynamic Tank, or Structural Glass blocks.

This quest requires enough blocks to build the minimum 3x3x3 size tank with 2 valves.

Congratulations on completing Automaton!

Here's a final creative item to make your further journeys more fun!
After updating the pack, claim this quest to reload the quest database and any quest changes.

These transformers allow you to customize how your power flows around.

The transformer will accept MV tier and provide LV tier as an output.

The HV transformer will accept HV tier and provide MV tier as an output.

This is handy for running your primary power using HV wires, but having transformers step down the voltage to a lower tier for machines that don't require that much power (for example, cloches and powered lanterns).
Similar to the Improved Blast Furnace, the Coke Oven Advanced uses powered preheaters and steel-reinforcement to produce coal coke and creosote oil faster.

Xtones is another option for creative and aesthetic building blocks.

Start by crafting Xtone Tiles as a base, then combine these with various dyes and other blocks to create new blocks to build with.

This Bonsai Pot allows you to grow a cute little tree in a single block space.

Place appropriate soil in the pot by right-clicking on the pot with the soil in hand, then right-click on the pot with a sapling to plant your tree. Harvest the tree by right-clicking on the tree with an axe when it is fully grown.

You'll have a chance to get sticks, logs, leaves, saplings, or apples on each harvest.

Note: this pot cannot be automated and all Bonsai Pots require clear space above for the tree to grow.

The Hopping Bonsai Pot is an upgrade to the standard Bonsai Pot that allows the pot to automatically harvest the tree and output the items to an inventory below the pot.

This pot functions the same as the standard Bonsai Pot in all other ways.
Welcome to Automaton! Let's make your first day a good day.
Now that you've established your base and gotten some basic tools and items going, it's time to tech up and start making your machines work for you.

betterquesting:10.name:8: I Can Show You the World
betterquesting:10.desc:8: Time to explore...in style.
Let's start shrinking your machines.
It's about time you got industrial about your resource gathering.
Break out the nukes.
